findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify which breaker is being removed: name the existing per-pass acting-fraction/blast-radius guard (classify.check_blast_radius, `reconciler.max_acting_fraction`) and state explicitly whether the new three-consecutive endpoint-family fuse REPLACES it or is ADDITIVE — and if replacing, how mass-change (blast-radius) protection is preserved.
evidence: Plan: 'Remove the rolling 5-of-10 breaker. An endpoint family opens after three consecutive exhausted eligible logical outcomes…'
search_files('5-of-10') and search_files('of 10') return no matching breaker in src/

classify.py:290 '── circuit breaker (pure…' and binding_walk.py:235 'circuit breaker over the WHOLE pass, BEFORE any mutation' — the existing breaker is check_blast_radius over acting FRACTION (default 0.10)

docs/jira-sync-setup.md:644 'gated by reconciler.max_acting_fraction (default 0.10): if the pass's acting decisions would exceed that fraction … refused before the first mutation' — a mass-change guard, not an endpoint-failure window
findings.finding: The plan removes a breaker described as 'rolling 5-of-10' that does not exist in the codebase; the actual reconciler breaker is a per-pass acting-fraction (blast-radius) guard that refuses a mass-retire/mass-mutate pass before the first mutation, which is a DIFFERENT concern from the new endpoint-failure fuse. If the fuse replaces the blast-radius breaker, mass-change protection is dropped.
findings.location: Approved policy: 'Remove the rolling 5-of-10 breaker.' / Acceptance Criteria line 4 (scoped fuse)
scenarios: A fetch/JQL regression empties the observation window and the coordinator would mass-retire/mass-mutate — the acting-fraction breaker is meant to refuse this, but the endpoint-failure fuse (three consecutive exhausted outcomes) never fires because the operations SUCCEED (they are just wrongly scoped).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the acting-fraction blast-radius breaker as an orthogonal mass-change guard and describe the new endpoint-family fuse as an additional failure-exhaustion guard; correct the 'rolling 5-of-10' description to the actual mechanism the plan intends to remove or leave in place.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the reconcile.py behaviour-preserving extraction + guard-test re-anchoring to exactly ONE of S5 (3350) or S5 T2 (0f5d), and reduce the invariant in the other to a 'must not break' constraint referencing the owning ticket.
evidence: S5 (3350) inherited section: 'This ticket edits `reconcile.py`, which sits at **799 of the 800-line cap**, so it must perform a behaviour-preserving extraction'.
S5 T2 (0f5d) inherited section (verbatim identical): 'This ticket edits `reconcile.py`, which sits at **799 of the 800-line cap**, so it must perform a behaviour-preserving extraction'.

insectile-modest-martin close comment: 'copied verbatim into the descriptions of the two tickets that will actually touch reconcile.py: diamond-flavoured-esok (3350) ... postmodern-tangled-mollusk (0f5d)'.
0f5d file_impact includes reconcile.py ('Advance state and exit status from proven coordinator outcomes.') and test_recovery_write_boundary.py is the shared guard for both.
findings.finding: The inherited reconcile.py pre-observation repair-boundary invariant (including the '799 of the 800-line cap' precondition and the mandatory behaviour-preserving extraction with its two guard tests) is folded verbatim into BOTH child S5 (3350-90b1) and its subchild S5 T2 (0f5d-2a24, postmodern-tangled-mollusk), and both tickets declare reconcile.py in their file impact and mandate the same extraction. Two tickets cannot each perform 'the' single behaviour-preserving extraction of a file that is at 799/800: whichever lands first invalidates the other's stated precondition, and both re-anchoring the same two boundary tests risks double edits / conflicting re-anchoring of tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_recovery_write_boundary.py.
findings.location: child 3350-90b1-2651-4c50 (RP-03 S5), overlapping with its subchild 0f5d-2a24-91d2-4148 (S5 T2)
scenarios: S5 (3350) performs the extraction first; when S5 T2 (0f5d) lands, reconcile.py is no longer at 799/800 and its stated '799-of-cap' precondition and 'must perform a behaviour-preserving extraction' instruction no longer hold, leaving ambiguous which ticket owns the extraction.

Both tickets touch tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_recovery_write_boundary.py and independently re-anchor the boundary tests, producing conflicting edits or a relaxed assertion that silently loses the ordering discriminator.
findings.suggested_fix: Designate S5 T2 (0f5d), which advances state/exit through reconcile.py, as the sole extraction owner; in S5 (3350) replace the folded extraction mandate with a pointer to S5 T2 and a preservation-only assertion, so the '799/800' precondition and test re-anchoring live in one place.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a bounded jitter default (e.g., jitter in [0, N]s) so cumulative sleep stays within the 15s cap and tests are deterministic.

No stated maximum jitter magnitude; the 15s cumulative sleep cap interacts with unbounded jitter.
findings.finding: The jitter magnitude is left unspecified: 'fallback delays are approximately 2s then 4s with nonnegative jitter' states nonnegativity but no upper bound, so total cumulative sleep near the 15s cap could be nondeterministically approached and the executor must guess the jitter range.
scenarios: An executor picks a jitter range that pushes cumulative sleep over 15s, or tests become nondeterministic.
